title: The Fleet — overview
note: A simplified, opaque view of the fleet. The operator makes the judgment calls and wraps them in a toolkit of /fleet-* skills (a few shown) — the intelligent layer over the mechanical fleetc CLI — which (with the operator's own raw verbs) actuate fleetc; fleetc drives fleetd (the daemon, shown as one box — no internal state machines); fleetd actuates its external systems (a Tracker, a Forge), persists to the Ledger, works inside a Project (the worktrees), and spawns the Crew of cogs. For what fleetd persists (the domain types and every ledger table) switch to the Data model.

detail.summary: Drafts a new ticket to /fleet-ready-done (title, four-section body, duplicate check, blockers + convoy, Ready check), then creates it with `fleetc ticket new` on whichever tracker the project uses. For the admiral and the operator: files work, never dispatches it.

Creates a git worktree + branch for a ticket in its project's impl/ folder, forked off a given base (default: origin's default branch). Pure worktree creation — no ticket lifecycle. Run when producing a dispatch, then pass the path to `fleetc dispatch --worktree`; reconcile spawns the cog there (reconcile never creates worktrees).

Launches the current branch's ship: pushes it, drafts the MR title + description from the ticket and the branch's divergence from its base, then opens the MR via `fleetc launch` (fleetd's forge adapter opens it — GitLab or GitHub alike). Run from the worktree.

Answers the open review threads on the ticket's MR through `fleetc review` / `fleetc reply` (forge-neutral): proves each finding against the code before fixing it, proposes it or pushes back with evidence, defers nits to one follow-up. Count-gated; surfaces floating notes before declaring the MR clean.

Rebases the ticket's MR against its target. Clean divergence → triggers the forge's server-side rebase via `fleetc rebase` and exits (the sailor re-fires on the result). Conflict → resolves locally with project/code understanding and force-pushes. Escalates only when the conflict needs a product/design decision.

Settles the open proposals, re-judges the anchored tickets, keeps every ticket in the convoy it belongs to, and checks the fleet's pace against its deadlines and its machinery's health. One numbered action each with its fleetc command; acts only on the operator's OK. For the shipwright.

Six of the kit's /fleet-* skills are shown; the rest wrap fleetc the same way: /fleet-new-project, /fleet-bearings, /fleet-groom-convoy, /fleet-ready-done, /fleet-convoy-report, /fleet-cost-report, /fleet-publish, /fleet-inspect, /fleet-review, /fleet-repair, /fleet-propose, /fleet-yield. Every one lives in skills/.
On the Overview fleetd is one opaque box. Inside, its heart is a single scheduling loop (scheduler.rs::run) — the state machine below.

stateMachine.note: Verified against scheduler.rs::run. Each pass fires any ticker whose Instant deadline has passed, then blocks on the mpsc command channel for ≤500ms (Timeout → re-loop). poll is READ-ONLY (overwrites the in-memory liveness snapshot — no ledger write, no event); sync, live reconcile, and each client command are the single writer's writes — one transaction appending a CDC event. Each sync is followed by the health check on the project's git state and its guards: a miss holds the lookouts (and is logged as health_checked when it changes). A Disconnected channel (UDS server gone) breaks the loop. Cadences shown are the config defaults (5/300/60s), re-read live each pass.

Read once at launch. [forge] + [tracker] are required; everything else defaults. The cadences, caps, review levers, thresholds and dry_run are live: `fleetc settings set` overrides them with no restart.

rows.informs: Liveness-poll cadence (s): how often the in-memory cog snapshot refreshes.
Sync cadence (s): hydrate the ledger from the tracker + forge.
Reconcile cadence (s): converge intent against reality.
A convoy's rest (s) between captain passes, from the last one's finish.
true = plan + log only, execute nothing (the parity look).
Admirals convened at once, one per confirmed escalation (-1 = no cap, 0 = none).
Lookouts reviewing allied MRs at once, one MR each (-1 = no cap, 0 = none).
Lookouts reviewing our own MRs at once, apart from the allies' cap.
Review rounds a worker gets on its MR; past them with threads open, it escalates.
How long an MR's threads must hold still before a sailor answers them (0 = at once).
The project's own review skill, which every lookout runs (unset = /fleet-review).
The project's grooming skill, run by an admiral on each ticket it grooms (unset = /fleet-ready-done).
The project's read-only readiness check, before dispatch and at grooming (unset = /fleet-ready-done).
Activity age under which a cog counts as Active.
Age under which a cog is Quiet; beyond it → Idle / Dead.
Bind addr of the OTLP/HTTP receiver that fills telemetry.db.
Product's main checkout (relative to fleet.toml): owns the impl/ ticket worktrees and the lookouts' review/ worktrees; captains launch here.
Which forge adapter drives the MRs.
GitLab numeric project id, or GitHub owner/repo.
true = `fleetc arm` sets the MR to merge once its gates pass; false = arm refuses, the operator merges on the forge.

Tracker project; for Jira also the ticket-key prefix (PROJ → PROJ-12).
